The difference formula for cosine gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=1 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\ ϕ & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
